subject.title: [Feature]: Support multi-target cron delivery from configured target sets

question: Should cron delivery gain a first-class explicit multi-target contract now, and should named operator-managed target sets be included in that first version or deferred?
rationale: This adds a durable public cron/config/protocol surface and needs deliberate choices for partial failure, idempotency, audit records, webhook behavior, and target-set ownership; those semantics cannot be safely inferred from prior unmerged proposals.

options.title: Stage explicit targets first
options.body: Add an explicit per-job target list with per-target outcomes and reuse the current delivery/session-safe path, while deferring named target sets to a separately designed configuration surface.

options.title: Approve targets and named sets together
options.body: Define both the cron fan-out schema and a managed target-set registry in one product design, accepting a broader compatibility and operator-control surface.

options.title: Keep fan-out external for now
options.body: Do not add a core cron contract until maintainers identify a sufficient plugin or workflow seam that preserves native receipts, retries, authorization, and session awareness.

recommendation.title: Stage explicit targets first
recommendation.body: Add an explicit per-job target list with per-target outcomes and reuse the current delivery/session-safe path, while deferring named target sets to a separately designed configuration surface.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged cron payload work makes this the closest current implementation history for choosing the delivery-contract boundary.
